sources.title: DC BLOX: Huntsville Data Center (Alabama colocation) location page, version of 20 October 2026
sources.source_family: DC BLOX data center location pages
sources.summary: DC BLOX's Huntsville location page describes its Huntsville data center at 333 Diamond Drive NW, Huntsville, Alabama 35806, near Redstone Arsenal, the Marshall Space Flight Center and Cummings Research Park, in the present tense: 'DC BLOX serves the needs of the Huntsville business community and all of Alabama with a secure Tier III colocation facility equipped with high-speed connectivity to Internet Exchanges, other DC BLOX data centers, and public cloud providers', and 'The Huntsville data center offers colocation and network and connectivity'. The facility was designed and constructed for agencies and contractors handling Controlled Unclassified Information. Building specifications: 9,000 sq ft expandable up to 52,400 sq ft, up to 7,400 sq ft of tenant office space, precast concrete shell, 150 mph wind-rated structure; security includes perimeter fencing, a vehicle gate and a 24x7x365 manned security desk; power is expandable up to 13.5 MW critical load with N+1 generator and UPS backup and 24-hour on-site fuel storage; cooling is N+1 high-efficiency direct expansion with hot-aisle containment. The page header gives 2 Huntsville data centers 'Operational & in Development', 38,000 square feet and 9 critical MW 'Committed & Planned' for the market as a whole. Its structured data (LocalBusiness GeoCoordinates) publishes the facility coordinate latitude 34.7118221, longitude -86.6921541.
sources.date_semantics: The page's schema.org metadata gives datePublished 2018-08-31 and dateModified 2026-10-20T15:02:13Z, and DC BLOX's wpseo_locations sitemap (captured 26 October 2026, us-la-ms-al-ar-p4-dcblox-locations-sitemap-20261026) gives the same lastmod for this URL. The modification is bounded below by the Internet Archive copy of 16 September 2026 (us-la-ms-al-ar-p4-dcblox-huntsville-page-ia-20260916), which carries the earlier version (dateModified 2026-09-14) with different wording ('Reserve Your Huntsville Colocation Space Today', 'colocation, network and connectivity and cloud storage services'); the live capture of 26 October 2026 is the 20 October version. published_at records that version and is used as a publication-normalised observation that the Huntsville colocation facility is operating on 20 October 2026. It is not an opening date (DC BLOX announced the opening on 28 September 2018).

sources.title: DC BLOX: DC BLOX Announces Opening of Huntsville, AL Data Center (press release dated 28 September 2018)
sources.summary: DC BLOX's release of 28 September 2018 announces the opening of its data center facility in Huntsville, Alabama, deployed with a precast concrete design near the Redstone Arsenal in 22 weeks, and gives the facility location for its ribbon-cutting as 333 Diamond Drive NW in Huntsville. It says that on final build-out the facility would deliver 46,000 sq ft of data hall space and up to 15 MW of critical IT power (a 2018 plan, not current capacity).
sources.date_semantics: Dateline 28 September 2018 (schema datePublished 2018-09-28; dateModified 2026-10-20 reflects a site-wide re-save). Identity and history context only: it ties the operating facility to 333 Diamond Drive NW. Not used for the status, which comes from the 20 October 2026 page version.

sources.title: Nebius: 'Ask Us Anything' - a public answer from Nebius on its Birmingham, Alabama project (dated 10.26, i.e. 26 October 2026)
sources.summary: A three-page Nebius document headed 'A PUBLIC ANSWER FROM NEBIUS 10.26' and linked from Nebius's Birmingham project page answers residents' questions about 'our project' in Birmingham: the facility will use a closed-loop cooling system and less than 1 million gallons of water a year, compared with more than 3 million gallons used by 'the Regions Facility that was previously located at the site'; Nebius pays the full cost of power and power infrastructure; it 'will have four backup generators on site'; a commissioned sound study shows operations will not exceed the ambient sound levels 'already present on Lakeshore Parkway'; the facility will employ at least 78 people; Nebius 'hosted a construction job fair on October 21'; and Nebius will pay an average of $85.7 million a year in taxes to the City of Birmingham, Jefferson County and the State of Alabama. It identifies the planned Nebius AI factory on the former Regions Bank back-office site off Lakeshore Parkway and describes it in the future tense; no permit, site work, construction or operation is stated.
sources.date_semantics: The document header reads '10.26' on every page. It is read as 26 October 2026: the asset URL carries cache-buster 2026-10-26T12:04:43.446Z, the PDF was created on 23 October 2026 (embedded CreationDate), and the text refers to a construction job fair held on 21 October as past. If '10.26' were instead read as October 2026, the document was still created on 23 October and publicly linked and retrieved on 26 October, so every reading places its publication between 23 and 26 October 2026, inside the window. published_at records 26 October; the status observation is the announced project on that day, not a construction start.
sources.pages_reviewed: pages 1-3 (pdftotext); first names of residents quoted in the questions are not reproduced

sources.title: Nebius: Nebius x Birmingham, Alabama project page (captured 26 October 2026)
sources.summary: Nebius's Birmingham project page says 'Nebius is developing the former Regions Bank back-office site in Birmingham's Oxmoor neighborhood for its potential AI factory' and 'We are in the planning stages for this AI factory'. Its timeline records 'September 2025 Nebius acquires 75 acres of land at 201 Milan Parkway in Birmingham's Oxmoor neighborhood' and lists permits, hearings, construction start (Q2 2026), initial-phase commissioning (Q4 2026) and build-out through 2028 as anticipated dates 'subject to change'. The FAQ says Nebius 'has received tax incentives for 30 years through the Industrial Development Board', that the project would connect to a new Nebius-funded switching station and substation from Alabama Power, and that Hoar Construction is the general contractor for a phased build of about 30 months. The page links the dated 'Ask Us Anything' document.
sources.date_semantics: The page carries no publication date. Nebius's server sitemap gives lastmod 2026-08-19T13:42:40Z, but the live capture of 26 October 2026 adds an introduction linking the 26 October 'Ask Us Anything' document that is absent from the Internet Archive copy of 19 August 2026, so the live version's date is not established and the page is used for identity only. Its timeline dates are forecasts and are not observations.

sources.title: Entergy Arkansas: Entergy Arkansas announces enhanced partnership at Google West Memphis campus, delivering at least $500M in new savings for all customers (news release, 19 October 2026)
sources.summary: Entergy Arkansas announced 'a second phase of its service to support Google's presence in West Memphis'. The release says 'The project will fulfill Google's plan for data center buildings on the site and accelerate the ramp-up of the original announced project', and that the planned system upgrades, about $600 million of investment plus a power purchase agreement, all covered by Google, include a 1,000 MWh battery storage system at Driver Solar near Osceola and a 400 MWh system near Hot Springs (both expected online in 2028), a 440 MW (ac) solar purchase agreement from the Big Island solar facility under construction in Mississippi County, and 'Expansion of the Galet substation near West Memphis and construction of two new 230 kV transmission lines to serve the expanded data center campus'. Entergy Arkansas's chief executive says Google 'is increasing its investment in West Memphis and building on the significant success of its first phase'. The expansion contract will be submitted to the Arkansas Public Service Commission and, pending approval, has an expected in-service date in 2028.
sources.date_semantics: Release dated 19 October 2026 (byline 'Posted: Oct 19, 2026'; schema datePublished 2026-10-19T20:06:12Z, dateModified 20:14:25Z). Power-readiness context only: the grid works are planned and subject to Arkansas PSC approval, and no data-centre construction stage, completion or operation is taken from the release.
